rv.q: This play, and these two deeply experienced actors, do them proud.

The result is a taut, troubling tale that de-deifies a nearly mythic figure in U.S. History while at the same time giving voice to the millions the Founders didn’t include as equals even as they declared independence and equality for all.
Their fact-based story is brilliantly told in Charles Smith’s The Reclamation of Madison Hemings at American Blues Theater.

It’s a compassionate and thoughtful bit of historical fiction that ultimately succeeds at centering those too often forgotten in our fetishizing of Great Man narratives and whitewashing of our sordid history.
Although the first act sizzles, Act II feels a little slow and sometimes tedious.
This is an imperfect play, though an interesting one.
This is a magical production that will hold you from start to finish!

cn.t: Critics praise Charles Smith's moving historical drama for its lively debates about freedom and identity, with strong performances bringing emotional depth to the story of Jefferson's enslaved son Madison Hemings and his journey to Monticello.
